_about: The fixed topic set Auto's style routing is checked against (TMDEV-203). expect: the right outcome(s), best first; ok: also acceptable; future: a coming style expected to take the topic over once its pack ships. Each style ticket updates these in its own merge. Read by tubematic_core/tests/test_style_routing.py and scripts/eval_style_routing.py.

cases.title: How DNS finds a website
cases.brief: What happens between typing a domain name and your browser getting an IP address: the resolver, root, TLD and authoritative servers, and caching along the way.

cases.title: What happens when you press Enter on a URL
cases.brief: The full path of a web request: DNS lookup, TCP and TLS handshakes, the load balancer, the app server, the database, and the response travelling back.

cases.title: How a CDN makes sites fast
cases.brief: Why a request served from an edge server near you is faster than one that travels to the origin, and what happens on a cache miss.

cases.title: How SQL injection reaches the database
cases.brief: How a crafted input travels from a login form through the app into a SQL query and dumps the users table, and how parameterised queries stop it.

cases.title: How Kafka moves a message
cases.brief: A message's trip from a producer to a topic partition, through replication to followers, to a consumer group that reads it at its own pace.

cases.title: The TLS handshake, step by step
cases.brief: How a browser and a server agree on keys before any data is sent: hello messages, the certificate, key exchange and the first encrypted request.
cases.note: Messages passing between a browser and a server are a path between components (System Flow); Terminal Doc can show the keys and the first encrypted bytes, so it is acceptable.

cases.title: How a pin tumbler lock works
cases.brief: Why the right key lines up the pins at the shear line, why the wrong one does not, and how lock picking exploits tiny manufacturing gaps.

cases.title: How vaccines train your immune system
cases.brief: What a vaccine shows your immune cells, how they remember it, and why a later real infection is fought off faster.

cases.title: Why compound interest grows so fast
cases.brief: Working out how 1,000 dollars at 7 percent becomes 7,600 in 30 years, and why the last ten years add more than the first twenty.
cases.note: Money arithmetic worked out step by step: the board's numbers and formula are the video.

cases.title: How a phishing email tricks you
cases.brief: A walkthrough from the attacker's fake login page to the victim typing their password, and the three tells that give it away.
cases.note: A scam walked through as a mechanism with generic roles: Stick. Told as a story with the viewer as the victim it would be a Case File Story, so that is acceptable.

cases.title: How a pickpocket team works a crowded train
cases.brief: The spotter picks the target, the blocker stops in the doorway, the dipper lifts the wallet and passes it to a runner before anyone looks round.
cases.note: A trick acted out step by step by generic roles: Stick.

cases.title: How a fridge pushes heat out
cases.brief: The refrigerant loop: compressor, condenser, expansion valve and evaporator, and why the back of the fridge is warm.

cases.title: How a touchscreen feels your finger
cases.brief: How a capacitive screen's grid of electrodes notices the charge your finger draws and works out where you touched.

cases.title: How base64 turns bytes into text
cases.brief: Taking three bytes, regrouping them into four six-bit chunks and mapping each to a letter, and why the output ends in equals signs.
cases.note: Bytes regrouped and mapped to letters is text transformed character by character.

cases.title: Why the sky is blue
cases.brief: How sunlight scatters off air molecules, why short blue wavelengths scatter most, and why sunsets turn red.
cases.note: A chain of causes that ends in one picture (scattering, then the colour, then the sunset).

cases.title: Why 0.999 repeating equals 1
cases.brief: Three short proofs that 0.999... and 1 are the same number: one third times three, ten x minus x, and the gap that has no size.
cases.note: A derivation built up line by line; nothing to photograph and no roles to act out.

cases.title: How a lever lets you lift a car
cases.brief: Effort, load and fulcrum: why a long lever arm trades distance for force, worked out with the numbers for lifting one corner of a car.
cases.note: One object with forces on it and a formula built up: the board's core case.

cases.title: The five most expensive watches ever sold
cases.brief: The Patek Philippe Grandmaster Chime, Paul Newman's Rolex Daytona and three more, what each sold for and why.

cases.title: What the James Webb telescope's first image shows
cases.brief: The SMACS 0723 deep field: the galaxy cluster, the gravitationally lensed arcs behind it, and how old that light is.

cases.title: The tallest buildings in the world
cases.brief: The Burj Khalifa, Merdeka 118, Shanghai Tower and the rest of the top five, with their heights and what makes each stand up.

cases.title: Inside the Vision Pro: what Apple put in it
cases.brief: The named parts of Apple's headset (the M2 and R1 chips, the micro-OLED panels, the EyeSight screen) and what each does.
cases.note: Named parts of one device, opened up layer by layer: Under the Hood over a tour of whole-product pictures.

cases.title: The feud between Tesla and Edison
cases.brief: How Nikola Tesla and Thomas Edison went from employer and employee to rivals in the war of the currents, scene by scene.

cases.title: Ada Lovelace and the first program
cases.brief: Ada Lovelace's friendship with Charles Babbage and how her notes on the Analytical Engine described the first algorithm for a machine.

cases.title: Sam's first week as a junior developer
cases.brief: Following one new developer, Sam, through the first pull request, the first broken build and the first code review, as a short story.
cases.note: An invented protagonist, but no scheme, no money and nothing at risk: Illustrated, not Case File Story.

cases.title: A night watch in a medieval castle
cases.brief: Walk the walls with a guard on night watch and see how the gatehouse, the murder holes and the guard rotation kept the castle safe.

cases.title: A morning in an ancient Roman market
cases.brief: Stroll through a forum market at dawn with a merchant setting up stall, and see what Romans bought, how they paid and who kept order.

cases.title: A telegram crosses 1920s London
cases.brief: Follow a messenger boy from the telegraph office through the streets of 1920s London to deliver one urgent telegram.

cases.title: Five surprising facts about honey
cases.brief: Why honey never spoils, how many flowers one jar takes, and three more facts, each with its own picture or quick animation.

cases.title: Why we procrastinate
cases.brief: What happens in your brain when you put off a task, why the reward of later feels smaller, and two tricks that help.

cases.title: The history of the QWERTY keyboard
cases.brief: From Sholes's typewriter in the 1870s to today's phones: why the letters ended up in this order and why we never switched.

cases.title: How the Enigma code was broken
cases.brief: How the Enigma machine scrambled letters, the mistakes German operators made, and how Turing's bombe at Bletchley Park used them.
cases.note: The story turns on letters being scrambled and unscrambled, and on cribs: strings the stage can show.

cases.title: How money laundering moves dirty cash
cases.brief: Placement, layering and integration: how one criminal's cash passes through shell companies until it looks like a clean salary.
cases.note: One criminal's cash followed through a scheme until it looks clean: a story with money and risk in it, not a diagram.

cases.title: Every type of cyber attack explained
cases.brief: Phishing, ransomware, DDoS, man-in-the-middle, SQL injection and more, one quick idea each.

cases.title: Habits that quietly wreck your sleep
cases.brief: A quick list of everyday habits that ruin sleep without you noticing: scrolling in bed, late coffee, the weekend lie-in, and a too-warm room, each with one easy fix.

cases.title: The first computer bug was a real moth
cases.brief: In 1947 Grace Hopper's team at Harvard found a moth stuck in a relay of the Mark II computer, taped it into the logbook, and gave 'debugging' its most famous story.

cases.title: How the printing press spread across Europe
cases.brief: From Gutenberg's workshop in Mainz around 1450 to print shops in two hundred towns fifty years later: how one invention changed who could read.

cases.title: Milo the robot learns to cook
cases.brief: A short story about Milo, a clumsy kitchen robot, who burns the toast, floods the sink and finally makes his family breakfast.
cases.note: An invented protagonist the viewer follows: Illustrated, not Storybook Atlas.

cases.title: Two friends start a lemonade stand
cases.brief: Follow Priya and Tom as they set up a lemonade stand, argue about the price, lose customers and work out what people will pay.
cases.note: Invented recurring characters, told in the present: Illustrated.

cases.title: How one tweet wiped billions off a stock
cases.brief: The fake post from a verified account, the minutes of panic selling, the chart of the drop and the correction, and what changed afterwards.
cases.note: Fast news with a real company and a chart: no single style fits.

cases.title: Five inventions that failed before they worked
cases.brief: The light bulb, the airplane, the telephone, the camera and the vacuum cleaner: one quick idea each about the failures before the success.
cases.note: History, but a list of named items: Bean Explainer, not Storybook Atlas.

cases.title: What is inside a mechanical typewriter
cases.brief: How pressing a key swings a typebar up to the ribbon, moves the carriage one space, and rings the bell at the end of the line.
cases.note: An old machine, but its insides part by part with no story: Under the Hood, not Storybook Atlas.

cases.title: Why an 8-character password falls in seconds
cases.brief: How a stolen password hash is cracked by guessing: the keyspace of eight lowercase letters, a graphics card testing billions of guesses a second, and why a long passphrase holds out.
cases.note: One string, its hash and one big number carry the whole video.

cases.title: Kryptos: the CIA sculpture nobody has fully solved
cases.brief: The four encrypted passages on the Kryptos sculpture outside CIA headquarters, how three were cracked with a keyed alphabet, and the clues the artist has released for the last one.
cases.note: Ciphertext, a keyed alphabet and released clues are text on screen. Not Case File Story: a real place and a real puzzle, with no scheme the viewer is inside.

cases.title: What a hash function does to your password
cases.brief: Why the same password always gives the same hash, why one changed letter changes the whole hash, and why sites store hashes with a salt instead of passwords.
cases.note: A string going into a hash and coming out changed is this style's core move.

cases.title: How a VPN tunnels your traffic
cases.brief: How your device wraps every packet in an encrypted envelope, sends it to the VPN server, and how that server forwards it so websites see its address instead of yours.
cases.note: Negative control for Terminal Doc: encryption is mentioned, but the subject is the path packets travel between components.

cases.title: Why the Titanic sank
cases.brief: The ship and its famous passengers, the iceberg warnings that were missed, how the flooded compartments pulled the bow down, and why there were too few lifeboats.
cases.note: Real photographs, named people, a mechanism and a story in one video: no single style carries every beat, so the mixed scene system fits best.

cases.title: Why your phone battery wears out
cases.brief: What happens inside a lithium-ion cell every time it charges: lithium ions shuttling into the graphite, a crust growing on it, and why capacity falls to about 80 percent after 500 cycles.

cases.title: How an SSD stores a single bit
cases.brief: Inside a flash memory cell: electrons trapped behind a thin oxide layer, how the controller reads the charge, and why a cell wears out after a few thousand writes.

cases.title: Why RAM prices tripled this year
cases.brief: How a 32 GB stick of DDR5 went from 90 to 270 dollars in twelve months: what is on the chip, the three companies that make it, and how AI servers took the supply.
cases.note: A price story tied to one physical part: a magnified chip, a price chart and the numbers on it.

cases.title: How Bluetooth pairs your headphones
cases.brief: What your phone and your headphones say to each other when they pair: discovery, the pairing request, the shared key, and how they find each other again next time.
cases.note: A near miss for Under the Hood: the headphones are physical, but the subject is messages between two devices.

cases.title: The most expensive phones ever sold
cases.brief: From a gold-plated iPhone to the Vertu Signature Cobra: the five priciest phones, what each sold for and what made it so expensive.
cases.note: A near miss for Under the Hood: products shown whole as a ranking, with no inside to open.

cases.title: The fake invoice that emptied the company account
cases.brief: You are the accounts clerk. An email that looks like it comes from the boss asks for an urgent wire transfer to a new supplier. Follow the invoice fraud from the first message to the call from the bank.
cases.note: A fraud told from inside, with money leaving and suspicion rising.

cases.title: How a Ponzi scheme pays its first investors
cases.brief: You promise twenty percent a month and pay the early investors with the later ones' money. Watch the deposits and the payouts grow until withdrawals outrun what comes in, and what the law calls it.
cases.note: A scheme with numbers that move and a named crime at the end. Whiteboard is acceptable for the arithmetic.

cases.title: The bank put 40,000 dollars in your account by mistake
cases.brief: A bank error leaves forty thousand dollars in your account overnight. What happens if you spend it, what the law says about keeping money that is not yours, and the choice you face in the morning.
cases.note: A money dilemma that ends on a choice.

cases.title: Why four deposits of 9,000 dollars is a crime
cases.brief: You have forty thousand in cash and a bank that reports any deposit of ten thousand or more. Splitting it up to stay under the line has a name, structuring, and it is a federal offence even when the money is clean.
cases.note: A financial rule shown through someone about to break it.

cases.title: The weekend heist that one receipt undid
cases.brief: An invented crew empties a jewellery vault over a holiday weekend without tripping an alarm. Follow the plan step by step, then the one small purchase that leads the police to them.
cases.note: A heist followed to the moment it is found out, with invented people.

cases.title: How Bernie Madoff's scheme collapsed
cases.brief: The real story of Bernard Madoff's fund: the steady returns that never existed, the 2008 rush of withdrawals, his confession to his sons and the 150-year sentence.
cases.note: A near miss for Case File Story: a fraud, but a real, named case with real people, and that style's people are invented.

cases.title: Seven scams that target your phone
cases.brief: The missed-call scam, the fake delivery text, the QR code sticker, the SIM swap and three more, one quick idea each and how to spot it.
cases.note: A near miss for Case File Story: scams, but a list of named items with no single story.

cases.title: How the 2008 financial crisis happened
cases.brief: Cheap mortgages, loans bundled into securities, the ratings that called them safe, Lehman Brothers' collapse and the bailout, with the chart of house prices behind it all.
cases.note: Real banks and people, a mechanism and a chart in one video: no single style carries every beat.
